# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_extent — round 1: 3 siblings (extent / type / scope), all gated on full val vs concurrent control
- Changes (3 sibling candidates, one lever each, prompt.md system message):
  - cand_extent: added rule "graded on THREE copies whose row/col counts differ; discover real data extent at run time (ws.max_row/max_column, scan to empty), NEVER hard-code counts from the preview". Targets 374-9/347-49 value+missing-cell errors from hard-coded sizes.
  - cand_type: added TYPE-preservation rule (copy via openpyxl not pandas to keep int/date/str; exact integer arithmetic → write int; keep float only when fractional). Targets 374-9/418-29/347-49 float-where-int / str-where-float.
  - cand_scope: added "change ONLY cells your answer produces; never pad the range; expected output often fills FEWER cells than the range". Targets 347-49 over-write past end + changed-original-cells.
- Round 1 RESULTS (gated vs concurrent control, evidence_bar 0.0067, gate_threshold ~0.048):
  - cand_extent reward 0.54, gate_delta +0.04 (ABOVE evidence_bar, BELOW gate_threshold) → directionally positive but under bar. regressions [40467(real – not in control), 47484(NOISE – also dropped in control replicate)]. Net +0.02 vs seed while dropping a 1.0 task ⇒ a real ~+0.12 gain on failing tasks masked by ONE over-generalization regression on the fixed-range date task 40467.
  - cand_type reward 0.493, gate_delta −0.0067 → FLAT / at noise floor. Refuted as written (no measurable gain). Only regression 47484 = noise.
  - cand_scope reward 0.457, gate_delta −0.043 → HARMFUL (over-restriction made the agent under-fill). Refuted.
- Building on / refuted: cand_type (type-preservation as prose) and cand_scope (blanket "produce fewer cells") are REFUTED as written — do NOT re-test these forms. 47484 and 160-6 are the NOISE tasks (flip in byte-identical controls); never credit their per-task moves.
- Decision: book cand_extent = reject (basis gate). Next round REFINES extent, not grows it: the +signal is real but capped by a real 40467 regression that more trials cannot remove.
- Focus next round: cand_extent2 = NARROWED extent rule — writes stay exactly = answer_position (protects fixed-range tasks like 40467); only source READING/aggregation adapts to real extent. Expect to keep the failing-task gain and drop the 40467 regression → clear the bar.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.540 Δ=+0.020 · fixed={52216} · broke={40467, 47484}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_extent: rejected val=0.540 Δ=+0.020 -->

## Iteration cand_extent2 — round 2: NARROWED data-extent rule (ACCEPT)
- Change (prompt.md): kept the extent-generalization rule from cand_extent but scoped it — "when your answer aggregates/transforms a SOURCE block whose length can vary, detect real extent (ws.max_row/max_column, scan to empty); this affects only how you READ, the cells you WRITE stay exactly answer_position." Surface = prompt.md.
- RESULT (round 2, gated vs concurrent control ctl_null_i1, evidence_bar 0.0067, gate_threshold 0.0414): reward 0.5633, gate_delta +0.05 → ACCEPT, verdict_stable across both control refs. Only regression 53161 = NOISE (also dropped in control replicate ctl_null_i1r1). 40467 (the real regression that sank cand_extent in round 1) is NOT regressed by the candidate here — it flickered only in the control → the narrowing removed the over-generalization trigger, exactly as hypothesized in round 1's handover.
- Built on round 1 RESULT: cand_extent (+0.04, rejected, regressed 40467). The refinement kept the failing-task gain and dropped the 40467 regression, clearing the bar. Did NOT re-test refuted forms cand_type / cand_scope.
- Focus next round (round 3): try to STACK a second safe lever on the new champion cand_extent2 for more gain (candidate 32468/374-9 value errors are computation-hard and not reliably prose-fixable; the remaining honest headroom is small). If nothing beats the champion, keep cand_extent2 and seal.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.563 Δ=+0.043 · fixed={52216} · broke={—}.
<!-- cand_extent2: ACCEPTED val=0.563 Δ=+0.043 -->

## Iteration cand_extent2 — round 2: NARROWED data-extent rule (ACCEPT)
- Change (prompt.md): kept the extent-generalization rule from cand_extent but scoped it — "when your answer aggregates/transforms a SOURCE block whose length can vary, detect real extent (ws.max_row/max_column, scan to empty); this affects only how you READ, the cells you WRITE stay exactly answer_position." - RESULT (round 2, gated vs concurrent control ctl_null_i1, evidence_bar 0.0067, gate_threshold 0.0414): reward 0.5633, gate_delta +0.05 → ACCEPT, verdict_stable across both control refs. Only regression 53161 = NOISE (also dropped in control replicate ctl_null_i1r1). 40467 (the real regression that sank cand_extent in round 1) is NOT regressed by the candidate here — it flickered only in the control → the narrowing removed the over-generalization trigger, exactly as hypothesized in round 1's handover.
- Built on round 1 RESULT: cand_extent (+0.04, rejected, regressed 40467). The refinement kept the failing-task gain and dropped the 40467 regression, clearing the bar. Did NOT re-test refuted forms cand_type / cand_scope.
- Focus next round (round 3): try to STACK a second safe lever on the new champion cand_extent2 for more gain (candidate 32468/374-9 value errors are computation-hard and not reliably prose-fixable; the remaining honest headroom is small). If nothing beats the champion, keep cand_extent2 and seal.

## Iteration cand_e2_typecode — round 3: type-enforcement stacked on champion (INCONCLUSIVE)
- Goal: stack a second SAFE lever on champion cand_extent2 for extra gain, attacking the remaining prose-addressable failure mode (grader compares TYPE as well as value: float 25.0 fails an int-25 cell; "5" fails a numeric 5).
- Three siblings, all built FROM cand_extent2:
  - cand_e2_typecode (prompt.md): type rule as a concrete CODE recipe — openpyxl copy `dst[addr]=src[addr].value` (not pandas), collapse integral float `int(v) if isinstance(v,float) and v.is_integer() else v`, never number-as-string. (Different FORM from round-1's refuted type PROSE.)
  - cand_e2_verifytype (task_template.md, fresh SURFACE): strengthened the existing step-3 verification to print value AND `type()` and check int-not-float / not-text before finishing.
  - cand_e2_both: both edits stacked.
- RESULT (round 3, full val, 10 trials, k_se=1.0, gated vs concurrent control; two byte-identical control replicates ctl_null_i2=0.550, ctl_null_i2r1=0.573, evidence_bar=0.0233):
  - cand_e2_typecode reward 0.600: +0.050 vs ctl_null_i2 (accept, thr 0.024) BUT +0.0267 vs ctl_null_i2r1 (reject, thr 0.042) -> verdict UNSTABLE -> INCONCLUSIVE. Its edge sits inside the control-replicate gap; not resolvable at n=10.
  - cand_e2_both reward 0.577: +0.0267 / +0.0033 -> accept/reject -> unstable -> inconclusive (weaker).
  - cand_e2_verifytype reward 0.553: +0.0033 / -0.020 -> reject/reject -> STABLE REJECT. The template already had a verify step; adding type-checking prose to it did not move the metric.
- Booking: cand_e2_typecode as INCONCLUSIVE (charges iteration, not stall; kept out of rejected.jsonl — type-enforcement is not refuted as an idea, it just could not be resolved from re-measurement noise at this n). Champion UNCHANGED = cand_extent2 (0.5633).
- NOTE on round.py: this round.py invocation's console/round_i2.json aggregation emitted null rewards for all rows despite all 100/100 rollouts being written and fully scored per tag (verified directly + via gate_check.py). Verdicts above were computed with gate_check.py over the existing rollouts and confirmed by hand-paired diffs; no re-eval was run (re-running the same tags only REPLACES t0..t9, buying no evidence).
- For a future run wanting to pursue type-enforcement: it needs MORE trials (grow.py) to resolve a ~+0.03-0.05 effect below the n=10 noise floor, or a form that fixes the hard-computation tasks (32468/374-9/52216) which prose does not reliably reach.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** UNRESOLVED (not judged; champion unchanged) · val=0.600 Δ=+0.037 · fixed={53161} · broke={52216}. — the measurement could not separate this edit from re-measurement noise, so it is NOT evidence against the edit. Its batch was still reverted. To resolve it, re-measure it under a FRESH tag (re-running the same tag REPLACES its rollouts) or with more trials in ONE evaluation; do not redesign it on this round's numbers, and do not re-derive it as a new idea.
